claim: The Legislature convenes every year at 10 a.m. on the third Wednesday in January
quote: The legislature shall convene annually in regular session at 10:00 o'clock a.m. on the third Wednesday in January.

claim: Regular sessions are limited to sixty days, extendable by up to fifteen
quote: Regular sessions shall be limited to a period of sixty days

claim: The governor may call a special session
quote: The governor may convene both houses or the senate alone in special session.

claim: Presiding officers must convene a special session at the written request of two-thirds of each house
quote: At the written request of two-thirds of the members to which each house is entitled, the presiding officers of both houses shall convene the legislature in special session.

claim: Bills presented ten or more days before adjournment: governor has ten days
quote: The governor shall have ten days to consider bills presented to the governor ten or more days before the adjournment of the legislature sine die

claim: Bills presented late or after adjournment: governor has forty-five days after adjournment
quote: The governor shall have forty-five days, after the adjournment of the legislature sine die, to consider bills presented to the governor less than ten days before such adjournment, or presented after adjournment

claim: The governor must give ten days' notice of intent to veto such a bill
quote: unless the governor by proclamation shall have given ten days' notice to the legislature that the governor plans to return such bill

claim: The day counts exclude Saturdays, Sundays and holidays
quote: the following days shall be excluded: Saturdays, Sundays, holidays

claim: General elections are in November of even-numbered years
quote: General elections shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November in all even-numbered years.

claim: No voter may be required to declare a party preference to vote in a primary
quote: no person shall be required to declare a party preference or nonpartisan

claim: The primary is the second Saturday of August in even-numbered years
quote: The primary shall be held on the second Saturday of August in every even numbered year.

claim: Only candidates nominated in the primary may run in the general
quote: No person shall be a candidate for any general or special general election unless the person has been nominated in the immediately preceding primary or special primary.

claim: Each voter receives every party's ballot and the nonpartisan ballot, with no party declaration required
quote: No person eligible to vote in any primary or special primary election shall be required to state a party preference or nonpartisanship as a condition of voting.

claim: A voter may vote for one party's candidates or only nonpartisan candidates
quote: A voter shall be entitled to vote only for candidates of one party or only for nonpartisan candidates.

claim: The top vote-getter in a party primary is the party's general election candidate
quote: The person or persons receiving the greatest number of votes at the primary or special primary as a candidate of a party for an office shall be the candidate of the party

claim: A county office candidate who will be unopposed in the general is declared elected after the primary
quote: any candidate for any county office who is the sole candidate for that office at the primary or special primary election

claim: Nonpartisan candidates advance with 10 percent of the vote or the lowest nominated partisan vote
quote: Any nonpartisan candidate receiving at least ten per cent of the total votes cast for the office

claim: No one may sign nomination papers for more than one candidate for the same office
quote: No person shall sign the nomination papers of more than one candidate, partisan or nonpartisan, for the same office

claim: Every candidate files a nomination paper to appear on a primary ballot
quote: unless a nomination paper was filed on the candidate's behalf

claim: The Legislature creates counties and gives them powers by general law
quote: The legislature shall create counties, and may create other political subdivisions within the State, and provide for the government thereof.

claim: Each county may adopt a self-government charter
quote: Each political subdivision shall have the power to frame and adopt a charter for its own self-government

claim: Charter provisions on structure are superior to statute, subject to general laws
quote: Charter provisions with respect to a political subdivision's executive, legislative and administrative structure and organization shall be superior to statutory provisions

claim: Real property taxation is exclusively for the counties, except Kalawao
quote: shall be exercised exclusively by the counties, with the exception of the county of Kalawao

claim: The local government article does not limit laws of statewide concern
quote: This article shall not limit the power of the legislature to enact laws of statewide concern.

claim: The board of education is appointed by the governor with Senate consent
quote: The governor shall nominate and, by and with the advice and consent of the senate, appoint the members of the board of education

claim: The board of education sets statewide policy and appoints the superintendent of the public school system
quote: to formulate statewide educational policy and appoint the superintendent of education as the chief executive officer of the public school system
